name: @anclora/design-system
_agentReadme: This manifest is the machine-readable contract for coding agents working in any Anclora repo. Read componentStatus before adding a component (canonical = consume it, do not rebuild it; candidate = usable but not yet a hard requirement; needsConsumerEvidence = ships but has no confirmed real usage, verify before relying on it). Read profiles before choosing shell/density defaults for a new app. Read extensionPoints before overriding anything — if the property you need to change is not listed as a component's extension point, add a variant here instead of overriding the base selector. Read prohibitedPatterns before writing CSS that touches an .ac-* selector directly. Full architecture: ANCLORA-DESIGN-SYSTEM-ARCHITECTURE.md. Full evidence: docs/ecosystem-audit/.

componentStatus._note: canonical = at least one real consumer verified in code (see ANCLORA-DESIGN-SYSTEM-COMPONENT-INVENTORY.md). needsConsumerEvidence = shipped as CSS, no confirmed real usage found as of 2026-09-21 — usable as a candidate, do not describe it to a user as battle-tested.

P-MKT.name: Marketing / Landing
P-MKT.description: Public, unauthenticated, single-scroll narrative page. No persistent nav shell.

P-WKS.name: Workspace / Operational
P-WKS.description: Authenticated, persistent sidebar/topbar shell, high information density: tables, entity lists, forms, modals, status badges.
mayOverride: component density/size defaults (use .ac-button--compact, not a new class)

profiles._note: Full app-to-profile assignment: ANCLORA-DESIGN-SYSTEM-PRODUCT-MATRIX.md. An app with no strong shell/density need needs no profile ('Core / default' is valid) — do not force one.

button.note: --compact (0.5.0) is the canonical 'smaller/denser button for a workspace surface'. --icon (0.6.0) is the canonical square icon-only shape — composes with ANY variant and ANY density (e.g. `ac-button ac-button--ghost ac-button--icon` or `ac-button ac-button--secondary ac-button--compact ac-button--icon`); it is NOT a separate component, do not build '.icon-button'/'.table-action-button'/'.dashboard-icon-button' locally. An icon-only button MUST have an aria-label (or aria-labelledby) — the icon itself is never an accessible name, and a title/tooltip does not substitute for one. Do not use --icon for a toggle control that needs aria-pressed, or for a control that needs a specialized primitive (segmented toggle, etc.) — see prohibitedPatterns.

answersForAgents.I need a square icon-only button: Use `ac-button ac-button--<variant> ac-button--icon` (add `ac-button--compact` for the dense/36px version). Do not create a local class.
answersForAgents.Is .ac-button--icon safe against a local: Yes as of 0.6.0 — --icon uses a compound selector (.ac-button.ac-button--icon) specifically hardened against the cascade bug found in the anclora-talent Wave 1 pilot. --compact and the color variants are NOT hardened the same way yet; if this consumer has a local `.ac-button { ... }` override, scope it with :not(.ac-button--compact) etc. — see docs/ecosystem-audit/05-button-contract-hardening.md.

prohibitedPatterns: Overriding border-radius, font-size, font-weight, or text-transform directly on the bare .ac-button selector in a consumer app instead of using a --compact/--sm/--lg/--icon variant or an --ac-button-* custom property.
Building a local icon-only button class ('.icon-button', '.table-action-button', '.dashboard-icon-button', or similar) instead of composing `ac-button ac-button--<variant> ac-button--icon`.
Shipping an .ac-button--icon (or any icon-only control) without an aria-label/aria-labelledby, or relying on a tooltip/title as the accessible name.
Repurposing .ac-button as a toggle/pressed-state control (needs aria-pressed) or a menu/segmented-control primitive it wasn't designed for.

Creating a new parallel button/card/modal class family in a consumer app (e.g. '.app-button', '.dashboard-button') when a canonical .ac-* component with a suitable variant already exists or could exist as one — propose a variant here instead.
Redefining semantic tokens (--status-*, --danger, --success, --warning, --focus-ring) with app-local hex values instead of consuming the semantic layer.
Inventing a new theme-toggle mechanism (a fourth alternative to the data-theme attribute contract) in a new app.
Treating a shadcn/ui-generated component's default HSL/OKLCH palette as final without wiring it to Anclora's semantic/component tokens.
